items.excerpt: The Motion Picture Association and ByteDance signed a memorandum of understanding to protect film and TV intellectual property across ByteDance's generative products, covering the Seedance video models, Seedream image models, TikTok and more. It follows the February cease-and-desist over Seedance 2.0 deepfakes and sets the first studio-side guardrails for a mainstream video model.

Startup Mirage ran a daylong experiment broadcasting a 24-hour newscast in which AI-generated anchors covered real stories. Variety's dispatch is a reality check on how far continuous, unattended AI video production is from watchable craft.

Robin Williams' children revived his Instagram account as a hub for his legacy and a countermeasure to what they call the 'rampant AI abuse' of his likeness. It is a working example of estates using owned channels as posthumous likeness governance in the AI-slop era.

A new report goes inside Studio Ghibli as it plans its next film, names no successor to Hayao Miyazaki, and restates its position on AI. The studio's refusal of a master plan reads as a deliberate counter-model to AI-accelerated animation pipelines.

Animaze Montreal revealed its September 17-19 programming, including the festival's first-ever AI Animation Forum alongside a Bill Plympton retrospective. A major indie animation festival is formally putting generative pipelines on the main stage next to hand-drawn craft.

Filmmaker and AI executive Verena Puhm launched L.A.-based Matriarch, a production company developing AI-native and hybrid animation projects for its own slate and for third parties and brands. It is another sign that 'AI-native' is becoming a stated production model rather than a tool choice.

Seth MacFarlane's Fuzzy Door Technology ran its ViewScreen real-time visualization suite on Disney's live-action 'Moana,' feeding oceans, skies, a treasure cave and a 500-foot lava monster into the camera on set. Departments could judge blocking, lighting and framing against the finished world during the shoot rather than months later in post.

Allan Tepper tests Descript's translation and dubbing feature and finds it is not rotoscoping at all: the model encodes the speaker's face into a latent space and regenerates the lower half of the face so mouth movement follows the new language while lighting, teeth and identity hold. A concrete look at how generative visual dubbing now works inside a mainstream editing app.
